questions.q: Consider the following statements:\nStatement-I: The Indian Flying Fox is placed under the 'vermin' category in the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972.\nStatement-II: The Indian Flying Fox feeds on the blood of other animals.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.explain: Pteropus giganteus, commonly known as the Indian flying fox, is listed as a 'vermin' in the Indian Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, due to its destructive tendencies towards fruit farms. Hence, statement I is correct.\n\nIndian flying foxes maintain a frugivorous diet, supplementing it with insects as well as flowers, containing juice and nectar. Although their favorite fruits are figs, the animals also consume mango, guava, bananas, and various cultivated fruits. Hence, statement II is not correct.

questions.q:
With reference to India's Desert National Park, which of the following statements are correct?
1. It is spread over two districts.
2. There is no human habitation inside the Park.
3. It is one of the natural habitats of the Great Indian Bustard.
questions.explain:
Statement 1 is correct: Desert National Park is situated in the Indian state of Rajasthan. It covers an area of 3162 km² of which 1900 km² is in Jaisalmer district and the remaining 1262 km² is in Barmer district of Rajasthan State.

Statement 2 is not correct: There are 73 villages and settlements or Dhanis existing within the Park. These communities have inhabited this area for hundreds of years.

Statement 3 is correct: The DNP is one of the natural habitats of the Great Indian Bustard.

questions.q: Which one of the following National Parks lies completely in the temperate alpine zone?
questions.explain: The Valley of Flowers national park is located in the Chamoli district of Uttarakhand and is known for its meadows of endemic alpine flowers and the variety of flora. It lies completely in the temperate alpine zone.

questions.q: Which of the following are in Agasthyamala Biosphere Reserve?
options: Neyyar, Peppara and Shendurney Wildlife Sanctuaries; and Kalakad Mundanthurai Tiger Reserve
Mudumalai, Sathyamangalam and Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuaries; and Silent Valley National Park
Kaundinya, Gundla Brahmeswaram and Papikonda Wildlife Sanctuaries; and Mukurthi National Park
Kawal and Sri Venkateswara Wildlife Sanctuaries  and Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve
questions.explain: The Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve was established in 2001 and is spread across the two states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu. The reserve includes three wildlife sanctuaries, Shendurney, Peppara and Nayar, as well as the Kalakad Mundanthurai Tiger reserve.

questions.q:
Which of the following are the most likely places to find the musk deer in its natural habitat?
1. Askot Wildlife Sanctuary
2. Gangotri National Park
3. Kishanpur Wildlife Sanctuary
4. Manas National Park
questions.explain: The musk deer is most likely found in Askot Wildlife Sanctuary (also known as Askot Musk Deer Sanctuary), located in the Pithoragarh district of Kumaun, Uttarakhand and the Gangotri Wildlife National Park in Uttarkashi District of Uttarakhand in India.

questions.q: Which one of the following protected areas is well-known for the conservation of a sub-species of the Indian swamp deer (Barasingha) that thrives well on hard ground and is exclusively graminivorous?
questions.explain: Hard ground swamp deer (Barasingha or Rucervus duvaucelii), the state animal of Madhya Pradesh, is seeing a revival in the Kanha National Park and Tiger Reserve (KNPTR) after having been perilously close to extinction for a long time. KNPTR is on the Maikal range of the Satpura hills and is spread over an area of 940 square kilometers between the Mandla and Balaghat districts of Madhya Pradesh. The swamp deer is endemic to KNPTR.

questions.q: Among the following Tiger Reserves, which one has the largest area under Critical Tiger Habitat?
questions.explain: Nagarjunsagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve is the largest tiger reserve in India. The reserve spreads over five districts, Kurnool District, Prakasam District, Guntur District, Nalgonda District and Mahbubnagar district. The total area of the tiger reserve is 3,728 km2 (1,439 sq mi).

questions.q: In which one of the following States is Pakhui Wildlife Sanctuary located?
questions.explain: Pakhui Wildlife Sanctuary lies in the foothills of the Eastern Himalaya, in the East Kameng District of Arunachal Pradesh. It was declared a Tiger Reserve in 2002. The habitat comprises lowland semi-evergreen, evergreen, and Eastern Himalayan broadleaf forests.

questions.q: Which one of the following National Parks has a climate that varies from tropical to subtropical, temperate, and arctic?
questions.explain: Namdapha National Park is located in Arunachal Pradesh. It was declared as a tiger reserve under Project Tiger. The main vegetation of Namdapha is evergreen forests, moist deciduous forests, subtropical forests, temperate forests and alpine. It has a climate that varies from tropical to subtropical, temperate, and arctic.

questions.q: Which of the following National Parks is unique in being a swamp with floating vegetation that supports a rich biodiversity?
questions.explain: Keibul Lamjao National Park is the only floating park in the world. The Park is located in the southwestern part of Loktak Lake. The Loktak Lake has a unique ecosystem called 'Phumdi' (a Manipuri word meaning floating mats of soil and vegetation).

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Wetlands Conference of rivers
1. Harike Wetlands: Confluence of Beas and Satluj/ Sutlej
2. Keoladeo Ghana National Park: Confluence of Banas and Chambal
3. Kolleru Lake: Confluence of Musi and Krishna
Which of the above pairs is/are correctly matched?
questions.explain:
Pair 1 is correctly matched: Harike Wetlands is one of the largest man-made wetlands of northern India. It came into existence in 1952 after the construction of a barrage near the confluence of rivers Sutlej and Beas.

Pair 2 is not correctly matched: Keoladeo Ghana National Park is formed by the confluence of the Gambira and Banganga rivers.

Pair 3 is not correctly matched: Kolleru Lake is the confluence of Godavari and Krishna.
